ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are five congruent right isosceles triangles in the figure. They are arranged consecutively along the same horizontal line, with directions alternating up and down; the double arrow below marks the total horizontal length from the far left end to the far right end as 30 cm. Reasoning: This 30 cm is the sum of the horizontal side lengths of the five congruent triangles, so the length of the horizontal hypotenuse of each triangle is 30 ÷ 5 = 6 cm. If a right isosceles triangle has hypotenuse c, then the two legs are each c/√2, and the area is (1/2)(c/√2)^2 = c^2/4. Substituting c = 6, the area of a single triangle is 6^2/4 = 9 cm². There are 5 triangles in total, so the total area is 5 × 9 = 45 cm².

method.method_draft: From the image, identify that the five congruent triangles are arranged consecutively along one horizontal line, and the 30 cm dimension spans the combined horizontal sides of all five triangles. From the text, use that the five triangles are congruent right-angled isosceles triangles. Therefore each triangle has horizontal hypotenuse length 30/5 = 6 cm. For a right isosceles triangle with hypotenuse c, each leg is c/sqrt(2), so the area is (1/2)(c/sqrt(2))^2 = c^2/4. Thus each area is 6^2/4 = 9 cm^2, and the total area is 5 * 9 = 45 cm^2.
